evidence.content_invariant: A prover-aware check (grep for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom) finds zero declaration forms in any of these files. Every top-level form is either a bare rule-name symbol or a rule-name symbol followed by (fire-count try-count (:rule-class rule-name)) tuples: a rune-usage profiling report the certify-book toolchain writes to `.sys/` after certification, containing no theorem statement, definition, or proof of its own.
evidence.rationale: Remove exact declaration-free ACL2 certify-book useless-runes profiling sidecars from primary formalization search; they are generated build/certification cache output, not authored formal content.
review_evidence: All 6 files individually scanned end to end with grep -icE for defthm/defun/defrule/define/defsection/encapsulate/in-theory/defaxiom returning 0, and grep -c for '"' and ';' also returning 0, confirming bare-symbol/tuple format throughout with no declaration, string, or comment content.

Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
